content:
Apple's big September event is just around the corner, with the company set to unveil three new iPhone models: the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Ultra. Here's what to expect.

iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max

The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max will succeed Apple's popular 17 Pro lineup.

Rumoured features include:

  • A20 Pro chip with improved performance and efficiency
  • Major camera upgrades, most notably a variable aperture on the main camera
  • 35% smaller Dynamic Island for a more modern design
  • New colour options, headlined by a bold burgundy
  • The best battery life ever, with significant gains on the iPhone 18 Pro Max
  • Redesigned Camera Control button
  • Apple's in-house C2 cellular modem
  • New satellite features, including 5G support

The iPhone 18 Pro is also expected to command a higher starting price. Estimates suggest it could start at US$1,399, though I think it's more likely to be in the US$1,199 or US$1,249 range.

iPhone Ultra

The iPhone Ultra is said to be the name of Apple's first foldable iPhone, priced at over US$2,000, carving out a new premium tier.

The foldable design should make the iPhone Ultra the most groundbreaking model Apple has released to date. It will feature a wide book-style fold, with an outer display of roughly 5.4 inches and an inner display of 7.8 inches, similar to an iPad mini.

The build is expected to mirror the iPhone Air, with a titanium frame and a slim profile.

The iPhone Ultra will sport two rear cameras (main and ultrawide) and two front cameras, one for each display. Authentication will rely on Touch ID rather than Face ID.

Software will be the standout feature, with iOS 27 supporting side-by-side multitasking and landscape-adapted layouts that complement the new form factor.

Performance is expected to match the iPhone 18 Pro, also featuring the A20 Pro chip, along with a vapour chamber for cooling and the C2 modem.

The misses: iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2

As usual, September should also bring a new standard iPhone 18 and a successor to the iPhone Air.

However, reports suggest Apple is significantly reshuffling its autumn lineup this year, pushing the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 back to early 2027.

It's unclear whether this shift is purely strategic or simply a response to the current memory shortage. Either way, the absence of more affordable models means this autumn's new iPhone lineup will focus solely on the high end.

Are you planning to upgrade to a new iPhone this autumn? Which model will you go for? Let us know in the comments.
